Remnant Retribution

Pogo's explanation

This one is pretty straight forward and claude has done an ok job explaining it. What i would like to highlight is each nexus when destroyed will drop gate fragments that can be used to repair individual gates, so you dont have to do that whole text heavy quest line to use the gates, but you also just cant jump anywhere super early. You will need at least 2 gate fragments, one for each gate to actually jump anywhere.

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience

Standalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.

Threat Incursion — the threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds. Disrupt their supply chains and besiege the entrenched hives into decline.
Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.

Remnant Retribution
v0.3.1 - a late-game colony crisis - for Starsector 0.98a-RC5

Download

RemnantRetribution-0.3.1.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher.


Pogo's explanation

This one is pretty straight forward and claude has done an ok job explaining it. What i would like to highlight is each nexus when destroyed will drop gate fragments that can be used to repair individual gates, so you dont have to do that whole text heavy quest line to use the gates, but you also just cant jump anywhere super early. You will need at least 2 gate fragments, one for each gate to actually jump anywhere.


Claude's explanation

  • Destroying Remnant hulls anywhere in the sector builds the network's "grudge": frigate 1, destroyer 2, cruiser 4, capital 8, and Remnant Nexus 150 (the single biggest contributor).
  • As the grudge climbs, the crisis bar ticks up after every battle plus a monthly trickle, Remnant hunter-killer groups begin patrolling your systems, and a no-bombardment reconnaissance-in-force probes one of your colony systems as a warning shot.
  • The retaliation is a live, interceptable event: a strike force launches from the nearest surviving Nexus to saturation-bomb one of your colonies. Destroy it in your own system first and nothing is bombed.
  • Avert at the source - the moment a retaliation becomes impending, the marshalling Nexus's location is revealed on your map; destroy it before the fleet launches and the strike is cancelled outright.
  • Defeating a retaliation halves the grudge, but each strike you beat makes the next one stronger.
  • Roughly 8-15 live Nexus stations per sector; each one destroyed permanently scales down monthly progress, hunter-killer presence and strike strength, to a configurable floor (default 25%).
  • Destroy the last Nexus and the network converges for one final oversized strike (default 1.5x cap); defeat it to end the crisis permanently. Toggleable off for the classic eternal grudge.
  • Nexus loot, all on by default and individually toggleable: Gate Control Fragments that repair a single dormant Gate (the first repair also yields a Janus Device), a Domain-era planetkiller guarded by the last Nexus, and the option to hand the planetkiller to the Luddic Path for the permanent pather peace agreement.
  • For Starsector 0.98a-RC5. LunaLib optional (live in-game config menu; otherwise reads data/config/settings.json). Vanilla-only, no hard dependencies. Safe to add to an existing save; removing it mid-crisis breaks the save.


Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experienceStandalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.
  • Threat Incursion — the threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds. Disrupt their supply chains and besiege the entrenched hives into decline.
  • Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
  • Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
  • Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.
  • Useful Planetary Shield — planetary shields finally do something: they absorb orbital bombardment.

aiDescription: Introduces a dynamic threat system where the Remnant network tracks player aggression through a grudge mechanic. As the grudge rises, hunter-killer groups patrol systems and strike forces launch from Nexus stations to bombard colonies. Players can avert attacks by destroying the marshalling Nexus before launch or by defeating the strike force in their own system. Destroying all Nexus stations triggers a final, oversized strike that permanently ends the crisis.
saveCompatibilityText: Safe to add to an existing save; removing it mid-crisis breaks the save.
